newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Japanese emperor meets Argentina's Menem.
newsitem.headline: Japanese emperor meets Argentina's Menem.

text.p: Japan's Emperor Akihito and Empress Michiko exchanged warm greetings with Argentine President Carlos Menem on Tuesday, during a visit almost 100 years after the two countries established diplomatic ties.
The couple arrived on Monday afternoon as part of the first visit of a Japanese emperor and empress to Latin America. They also visited Brazil.

"It is a true honour for the people and the government of Argentina to receive you today and give you a most cordial and affectionate welcome," Menem told the couple, adding that 1988 would mark a century of bilateral relations.

Akihito replied: "My greatest wish is that we may strengthen our friendship and achieve a greater mutual understanding on the eve of the 100th anniversary of our diplomatic ties, which we celebrate next year."
Akihito and Michiko earlier were offered the keys to the city in a ceremony led by Mayor Fernando de la Rua.

During the event a group of teachers slipped through a security cordon and displayed a large banner in front of the imperial couple, written in Japanese, saying: "We have been on hunger strike since April 2 demanding a greater budget."
The couple arrived in Argentina after a 10-day visit to Brazil, home to the largest Japanese community abroad and the only other country they visited.
A dinner hosted by Menem was to be held on Wednesday night at an elegant downtown hotel, the Alvear Palace. Akihito and Michiko were due to leave the next morning for Japan.
